papers.title: The ecological adaptability of pinewood nematode populations: survival strategies, mechanisms and co‐evolution
papers.authors: Chen‐Xi Ying, Tong‐Yue Wen, Xiao‐Lei Ding, Xiao‐Qin Wu
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bursaphelenchus xylophilus (pinewood nematode, PWN) is the causal agent of pine wilt disease and ranks among the most destructive invasive pests threatening global forest ecosystems. Since its introduction to China, this nematode has triggered massive ecological and economic losses, while its distribution range continues to expand northward. The association between the widespread dispersal of B. xylophilus in invaded areas and the ecological adaptability of its populations has drawn considerable attention. RESULTS: This review systematically synthesizes recent research advances regarding the ecological adaptability of PWN populations, elaborating on molecular mechanisms and ecological strategies that enable the nematode to colonize novel environments. In terms of thermal adaptation, differentially expressed genes, small heat shock protein families and the accumulation of key metabolites collectively shape adaptive pathways to resist extreme high and low temperature stress. For host adaptation, PWN displays polyphagous feeding habits and relies on diverse arboreal fungi as nutritional resources when pines were weakened or died. papers.title: Application of Large Language Models in Agricultural Entomology
papers.authors: Pritha Ghosh, Ajinkya Markad
papers.abstract: Agricultural entomology, a critical field focused on the study of insects that affect crop production, benefits greatly from advances in artificial intelligence (AI), by using large language models (LLMs) such as Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer 4. These models, trained on large datasets, demonstrate remarkable natural language understanding and solution generation capabilities that can be used to address a variety of agricultural entomology challenges. LLMs make it easier to analyze large amounts of entomological literature, allowing researchers to quickly access and synthesize data on insect behavior, pest management strategies, and the ecological impacts of various species. LLMs can also help develop intelligent advisory systems that provide farmers with real-time, data-driven pest control recommendations, thereby improving sustainable agricultural practices. The use of LLMs in predictive modeling improves forecasting pest outbreaks by analyzing climate and environmental data. papers.title: Research Trends, Literature-Reported Occurrence Patterns, and Ecological Implications of Tuta absoluta in Agroecosystems of South China Karst
papers.authors: Yuyu Lu, Zihui Zhao, Kangning Xiong, Yuehua Song
papers.abstract: Biological invasions by non-native pest species can threaten agricultural production, biodiversity, and ecosystem stability. Tuta absoluta is a destructive invasive pest of tomato and other solanaceous crops. This review analyzed 97 eligible records published between 2010 and 2025 from the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) and Web of Science (WOS), combining scientometric analysis with systematic synthesis to examine research trends, reported occurrences, and potential ecological impacts. In South China, karst rocky desertification restoration zones are important for food production and ecological recovery, but their fragile environments may increase vulnerability to pest invasion. The results show a steady increase in related publications, with research themes shifting from field investigation and chemical control toward habitat suitability assessment, invasion mechanisms, ecological effects, and sustainable management. Literature-reported occurrences of T. absoluta in South China karst show a spatially heterogeneous distribution, with records concentrated mainly in parts of Yunnan, Guizhou, and Guangxi. papers.title: Effects of emerald ash borer specific gene silencing using RNA interference on soil communities
papers.authors: Faith Boa
papers.abstract: The emerald ash borer (EAB) (Agrilus planipennis Fairmaire) is an invasive wood- boring beetle from Asia that primarily feeds on ash trees (Fraxinus spp.). Since its invasion of North America, EAB threatens the functional extinction of ash with damages and management costs projected to reach $900 million by 2054. Current management strategies have been insufficient to prevent EAB’s spread, highlighting the need to advance innovative approaches like RNAi, which has demonstrated efficacy against EAB in laboratory and greenhouse trials. Double-stranded RNA targeting heat shock 70-kDa protein (hsp) induces EAB mortality, systematically disperses and persists in planta, and causes no phenotypic effects for several ash-associated insects. We evaluated the environmental and nontarget effects of dsHSP, focusing on soil communities. In laboratory soil incubation assays, dsHSP was recovered up to 8 h post-treatment. Exposure of the collembolan Folsomia candida to dsHSP-treated soil had no effects on adult survival or body length, but increased reproduction. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.authors: Munir Iqbal, Jiayun Yang, Elizabeth Billington, William T. Harvey, Sofia Riccio
papers.abstract: Abstract High pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) remain a major threat to animal and human health. The clade 2.3.4.4b H5Nx panzootic has been marked by increasing cross-species adaptation, including outbreaks in dairy cattle. The surge in mammalian infections in both wild and captive populations heighten concerns about zoonotic and pandemic potential. Here, we analyse haemagglutinin (HA) evolution in clade 2.3.4.4b H5Nx viruses from 2020 to 2025, focusing on key residues within the receptor-binding domain. We identify HA E185K (mature H5 HA numbering; E189K in H3 numbering) as a novel immune escape mutation that confers increased binding to avian- and human-type sialic acid receptors. Strikingly, this mutation is increasingly prevalent in cattle-derived H5N1 viruses and enhances binding to human-like receptors. However, ferret studies demonstrated that whilst pathogenicity of the E185K virus was comparable to the cattle derived isolate, the E185K mutation did not confer transmission to direct or indirect contact ferrets. papers.title: Consistent efficiency of horticultural intercropping: a quantitative synthesis
papers.authors: Julie Christine Scaloppi, Raphaël Paut, Camila De Toledo Castanho, Rodolphe Sabatier
papers.abstract: Abstract Agroecosystem diversification through intercropping is a strategy to mitigate biodiversity loss and enhance ecosystem services while maintaining or improving productivity, resource-use efficiency, and pest regulation. Although field crop intercropping has been well studied, horticultural intercropping remains less explored, despite its relevance for food security. Our study aims to address this gap by assessing the overall efficiency of horticultural intercropping through a quantitative synthesis of global experimental data. In addition, we examine how system design, management practices, and species characteristics influence land-use advantage. Our primary finding is that horticultural intercropping is advantageous compared with monocultures, providing the first large-scale, global quantitative evidence of a land-use advantage in horticultural systems. Overall, the mean Land Equivalent Ratio was 1.41, indicating that monocultures would require 41% more land than intercropping to achieve the same yield, with values exceeding 1 in over 90% of the experimental observations. papers.abstract: Campylobacter is a constant concern in ensuring food safety, as it is one of the most common pathogens in food. The main source of Campylobacter species in food is poultry meat, and the primary production of this meat is a critical point where measures need to be taken to reduce its presence in the food chain. Therefore, poultry slaughterhouses are recognized as places where it is necessary to implement measures to control and reduce the number of Campylobacter spp. Food business operators are obliged to ensure greater hygiene on the slaughter line, through the inspection of equipment for each step of slaughter and the application of regular cleaning protocols. Continuous monitoring of the presence and abundance of Campylobacter spp. on the slaughter line provides data on the validity of hygiene control measures in the slaughterhouse, as well as the data needed to assess the microbiological risk in poultry meat. Monitoring the presence of Campylobacter spp. in poultry slaughterhouses is a basic activity that is necessary for taking measures to reduce contamination, improve microbiological safety in poultry processing and thus improve the food safety system as a whole. The highly pathogenic strain MaCMUIPL 57 was subjected to virulence tests against different conidial concentrations. papers.abstract: Abstract Fosetyl-Al (aluminium tris-(ethyl phosphonate)) is a low-toxicity phosphonate commonly used to control oomycete-related diseases in crops. Trunk injection (endotherapy) delivers the fungicide directly into the vascular system, potentially improving efficacy while reducing environmental risks. This two-year study evaluated the efficacy and phytotoxicity of trunk-injected fosetyl-Al to manage ink disease caused by Phytophthora cinnamomi in Castanea sativa saplings. Fifty saplings received fosetyl-Al injections at 0–4% using pressurized devices, followed by stem inoculation with the pathogen; a 2% soil irrigation treatment was included for comparison. Trunk injections at 1%, 2% and 4% significantly suppressed stem necrosis and reduced root infections compared to irrigation and untreated control, with protection persisting for at least two years as reflected by reduced relative Area Under the Disease Progress Curve (rAUDPC) values. papers.abstract: Background: This research presents a critical analysis of mycotoxins produced by fungi, particularly the Fusarium genus, which is prevalent in cereal-producing regions. Given the global impact of mycotoxins on food safety and animal health, this study addresses an urgent issue in agricultural science. It highlights the various environmental, physical, and biological factors influencing mycotoxin production, providing valuable insights for developing effective management strategies. The study also discusses the health risks associated with specific mycotoxins, such as zearalenone and fumonisins, which have been linked to serious health issues in both animals and humans. Furthermore, it emphasizes the need for ongoing prevention and control programs to mitigate mycotoxin contamination in the food chain. By exploring analytical challenges and proposing future directions for research and policy, this work contributes significantly to the understanding of mycotoxin dynamics in agricultural systems. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.source: OpenAlex / Digital Commons - USU (Utah State University)
papers.abstract: Beef cattle grazing systems in the western United States often depend on grass monocultures that decline in nutritional quality during summer. As pasture quality decreases, cattle have fewer opportunities for selective foraging, grazing efficiency declines, and producers face increased supplementation costs to maintain animal performance, welfare, and effective pasture use. This dissertation examined whether interventions that provide phytochemicals either as a supplement or through the establishment of taxonomically diverse “hot spots” in otherwise monotonous landscapes could improve cow-calf pair performance and enhance the sustainability of agroecosystems. The study tested two strategies with free-grazing cow–calf pairs: supplementation with tannin extract and establishing of small patches, or “islands,” of diverse, phytochemically rich forage species within bromegrass pastures. Using combined GPS–tri-axial accelerometer collars, pedometers, and machine-learning methods, the study identified cattle behavioral responses to these feeding strategies with high accuracy. papers.authors: Amit K. Chakraborty, Hao Wang, Pouria Ramazi
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of The Royal Society Interface
papers.abstract: Abstract The equations of complex dynamical systems may not be identified by expert knowledge, especially if the underlying mechanisms are unknown. Data-driven discovery methods address this challenge by inferring governing equations from time-series data using a library of functions constructed from the measured variables. However, these methods typically assume time-invariant coefficients, which limits their ability to capture evolving system dynamics. To overcome this limitation, we allow some of the parameters to vary over time, learn their temporal evolution directly from data and infer a system of equations that incorporates both constant and time-varying parameters. We then transform this framework into a forecasting model by predicting the time-varying parameters and substituting these predictions into the learned equations. The model is validated on simulated susceptible–infected–recovered and consumer–resource systems, as well as on real-world greenhouse gas concentration and cyanobacteria cell count datasets. papers.title: HMTS-YOLO: Detection of Weed Apex and Root/Stem-Base Treatment Regions for Precision Laser Weeding
papers.authors: Yihua Chen, Meng-Di Yuan, Liming Qin, Qian Hu, Simon X. Yang
papers.abstract: Abstract Under complex field backgrounds, weed apex and root treatment regions are readily affected by soil texture, surface cracks, target-scale variation, and morphological differences, resulting in missed detections, false detections, and bounding-box regression errors, particularly for small-scale and elongated targets. To improve dual-class treatment-region detection for field weeds, a dataset comprising 4,582 images and 13,421 bounding boxes was curated from existing field images and treatment-region annotations, and HMTS-YOLO (Hierarchical Morphology-aware Texture-Suppression YOLO) was developed using YOLOv8s as the baseline. The proposed model introduces STS-C2f, LDM-C2f, and DMA-SPPF at the P2, P3, and P5 feature levels, respectively. papers.authors: Yajie Sun, Ali Zia, Vivien Rolland, Charissa Yu, Jun Wei Zhou
papers.abstract: Spectral 3D computer vision combines wavelength-resolved measurements with geometric information to support material-aware reconstruction, perception, and scene analysis. However, the literature remains fragmented across hyperspectral and multispectral sensing, cross-spectral depth and pose estimation, spectral point clouds, LiDAR–hyperspectral fusion, and neural scene representations. This survey provides a structured review of the field, covering spectral and geometric acquisition, data representations, calibration and registration, spectral 3D reconstruction, integrated spectral 3D acquisition and joint physical modelling, learning-based methods, downstream tasks, benchmark datasets, applications, and software tools. We organise existing methods into three complementary methodological themes: spectral support for 3D information estimation, spectral 3D reconstruction and mapping, and integrated spectral 3D acquisition and joint physical modelling. papers.authors: Timothy P Lampasona, Cesar Rodriguez‐Saona, Anne L. Nielsen
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Plum curculio, Conotrachelus nenuphar (Herbst), is a native fruit pest. Adults emerge from overwintering sites in wooded areas and disperse into crop fields in the spring. However, their movement patterns within fields after this initial dispersal remain poorly understood. In this study, we used protein markers to investigate the in‐field dispersal of C. nenuphar adults in peach ( Prunus persica L.) and highbush blueberry ( Vaccinium corymbosum L.) fields. Chicken egg albumin (egg whites) was applied along field borders and bovine casein (cow's milk) within field interiors. Adults were collected daily using beat sampling, and enzyme‐linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA) were used to detect egg and/or milk proteins on individual insects. This approach provided a form of behavioural forensics, allowing us to trace each insect's movement within the field. Results indicated a strong edge effect in both crops, with 64.3% and 78.0% of adults collected along the border in blueberry and peach, respectively. papers.title: Optimal Control Analysis and Cost‐Effectiveness Calculations of Chickenpox Transmission Dynamics
papers.authors: Ahuod S. Alsheri, Hegagi Mohamed Ali, Essam M. Elsaid, Mohamed Rabea Eid, W. S. Hassanin
papers.source: OpenAlex / Optimal Control Applications and Methods
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study develops and analyses a mathematical model for chickenpox transmission dynamics. The model's basic properties, including positivity, boundedness, and stability of disease‐free and endemic equilibria, are rigorously established. The basic reproduction number is derived, and sensitivity analysis identifies the most sensitive parameters. An optimal control problem is formulated with four time‐dependent controls (preventive measures, vaccination, pharmaceutical interventions, and non‐pharmaceutical treatments). Numerical simulations using a forward‐backward sweep method (FBSM) are conducted. Several control scenarios that resulted from the intersection of the recommended controls to clarify the impact of these controls and explore the most effective way to halt the disease's progress are presented. Moreover, the cost‐effectiveness analysis is presented to offer a quantitative comparison between the suggested five control scenarios. papers.title: Integrated School-Based Education for the Control of Overweight and Obesity among Adolescents in Bulukumba, Indonesia: A Quasi-Experimental Study
papers.authors: Asnidar Asnidar, Muriyati Muriyati, Fitriani Fitriani, Asdinar Asdinar, Anggriani Anggriani
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Overweight and obesity among adolescents are public health problems that may persist into adulthood and increase the risk of non-communicable diseases. School-based health education can support behavioural change; however, the integration of the School Health Unit (UKS) with primary healthcare services has not been optimal. This study evaluated an educational approach integrating researchers, school UKS managers, and UKS programme coordinators at Puskesmas. Methods: This study employed a quasi-experimental design with a pretest-posttest control group approach involving 210 adolescents with overweight or obesity from 21 junior secondary schools within the service areas of 21 Puskesmas in Bulukumba Regency. The participants comprised 105 adolescents in the intervention group and 105 in the control group. The intervention group received integrated education accompanied by an educational module, whereas the control group received the module for self-directed learning. Knowledge was measured using a 20-item questionnaire; physical activity using the Physical Activity Questionnaire for Adolescents (PAQ-A); dietary intake patterns using a Food Frequency Questionnaire

papers.abstract: Introduction Antibiotic resistance is spreading throughout aquatic ecosystems, especially wetlands that receive urban and industrial effluents. These environments are large reservoirs under anthropogenic selection pressure, favouring the persistence and transmission of multidrug-resistant (MDR) diseases. This study investigated the biofilm-forming capacity and antimicrobial resistance profiles of 32 environmental bacterial isolates recovered in 2024, assessing the microbiological water quality of a sewage-fed aquaculture unit within the East Kolkata Wetlands (EKW), an Indian Ramsar site. Methods To characterise persistence-associated biofilm formation, phenotypic antimicrobial resistance, and hemolytic activity, isolates were evaluated using quantitative biofilm assays, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and blood-agar hemolysis profiling, respectively. We constructed a composite phenotypic risk score using a risk-quadrant approach to classify isolates based on the convergence of multidrug resistance, strong biofilm formation, and hemolytic activity. papers.title: Influence of Sustainable Agricultural Practices on Microbial Aspects of Soil
papers.authors: Dušan Adamov, Milica Vranešević, Dragana Stamenov, Simonida Đurić
papers.abstract: Abstract Soil is a non-renewable natural resource essential for supporting plants, animals, and microorganisms. The intensification of conventional agriculture has substantially affected soil health, including its microbial component. This review evaluates how sustainable agricultural practices, including crop rotation, intercropping, cover cropping, organic amendments, and agroforestry, influence microbial aspects of soil health, with particular emphasis on microbial biomass, diversity, community composition, and functions related to nutrient cycling. Peer-reviewed studies published up to 2025 were identified through Web of Science, PubMed, and Google Scholar using combinations of terms describing individual agricultural practices and microbial soil health parameters. The reviewed evidence indicates that crop diversification can enhance microbial biomass and modify microbial community composition through changes in soil properties, nutrient cycling, root exudation, and organic inputs, although responses vary among cropping systems and environmental conditions. papers.title: Mycobiota associated with diseased Schrenk’s spruce in mountain forest ecosystems of Kyrgyzstan
papers.authors: Tinatin Doolotkeldieva, Батма Жусупова
papers.abstract: Schrenk’s spruce ( Picea schrenkiana ) is a dominant coniferous tree species in the Western Tian Shan forests and plays an important ecological role in maintaining mountain forest ecosystems in Kyrgyzstan. In recent years, the Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve has seen a significant increase in diseased and declining spruce trees, raising concerns about forest health and ecosystem stability. The present study aimed to investigate the fungal communities associated with diseased roots, stems, and needles of Schrenk’s spruce in the Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve, Kyrgyzstan. We identified fungal isolates from symptomatic plant tissues using morphological characteristics, ITS (5.8S rRNA) sequencing, and species-specific molecular markers. Mycological analysis revealed a diverse fungal community associated with diseased spruce tissues. Penicillium and Talaromyces species were predominantly isolated from infected roots. Penicillium species were most commonly associated with needle lesions (approximately 50%), followed by Alternaria (20%), Curvularia (20%), and Didymella species (10%). papers.title: Effect of Drought Stress, Soil Salinity, P. indica, and MWCNs on Biodegradation of Diesel Oil in the Pb- and Cd-Polluted Soil Under Cultivation of Triticale Plant
papers.authors: , Amir Hossein Baghaie
papers.source: Crossref / Journal of Advances in Environmental Health Research
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Today, soil pollution with heavy metals and petroleum compounds is one of the main environmental problems. This research was done to investigate the effect of drought stress, soil salinity, Piriformospora indica (P. indica), and MWCNs on biodegradation of diesel oil in the soil that contaminated with Pb and Cd under cultivation of triticale plant. Methods: Treatments consisted of applying MWCNs (2% [W/W]) in the Pb- and Cd-polluted soil that was simultaneously polluted with diesel oil (0, 5, and 10% [W/W]), and the plants used in this study were inoculated with P. indica. After 70 days, plants were harvested, and plant and soil Cd were measured using AAS (atomic absorption spectrometry). In addition, the degradation percentage of diesel oil in soil was determined. Results: Soil application of MWCNs at the rate of 2% (W/W) significantly increased the biodegradation of diesel oil in the soil in the drought and salinity (6 dS/m) stress by 11.3% and 15.6%, respectively. In addition, plant inoculation with P. indica significantly increased the biodegradation of diesel oil in the soil by 12.3%. papers.title: Isolation and characterization of Candida palmioleophila from poultry slaughterhouse wastewater: a first report from Brazil
papers.authors: Enrico Mendes Saggioro, Gisela Lara da Costa, Beatriz Oliveira de Farias, Barbara Costa Pereira, Ramon Loureiro Pimenta
papers.abstract: Environmental fungi are increasingly recognized as emerging pathogens and potential agents for biotechnological applications. Candida palmioleophila, an ascomycete yeast originally isolated from soil, has demonstrated resistance to fluconazole and capacity for bioremediation of fats and pharmaceuticals. The Brazilian poultry industry produces large volumes of wastewater, which can serve as a reservoir for fungal species with pathogenic and environmental importance. In this study, we performed a fungal screening of wastewater from poultry slaughterhouses. Wastewater samples were collected from a poultry slaughterhouse in São José do Vale do Rio Preto, Rio de Janeiro. Fungal isolation was performed using Sabouraud Dextrose Agar supplemented with antibiotics. Only yeasts were obtained and identified by polyphasic taxonomy. Species identification of both isolates were confirmed by MALDI-TOF MS and ITS sequencing, and the antifungal susceptibility of the strains was evaluated using the Vitek2 system. papers.title: Leaving X: How scale insects repeatedly evolved alternatives to chromosomal sex determination
papers.authors: Andrew J. Mongue, Erin C. Powell, Tracy Liesenfelt, Ethan Grebler, Amanda Markee
papers.abstract: Abstract Reproduction is a core feature of life, yet it is still unclear why sex determination systems are conserved for hundreds of millions of years in some taxa but repeatedly turn over in others. A prime example is the true bugs; the vast majority of families employ a conserved X sex chromosomal system, but in scale insects (Coccomorpha), sex determination systems are more varied. Scale insects may retain X chromosomes, employ a form of haplodiploidy known as paternal genome elimination (PGE), or reproduce via selfing as simultaneous hermaphrodites. We sequenced 17 new scale insect species to study sex determination transitions. We recovered two independent losses of the X, once in the family Monophlebidae and a second time at the base of the PGE families. In the former, genomic rearrangements begin before the X is lost, leading to a pair of massive autosomes to which the X fuses in hermaphrodites.
